reason: The contradiction is real and I verified it by driving ?state=first-run: the hero reads 12 jobs finished since you started against a single hatched bar labelled 13 Jul at a reading of 09:14 Thursday 16 July 2026, and the same page renders movementTwo() unchanged — .ages head 'Oldest · 41 days', nine dots including 'Confirm the marquee sides with the hire company, open 41 days', three carrying .old, the scale running today/15d/30d/45d, and the spoken line '3 jobs have been open longer than a fortnight'. VIEW['first-run'] concatenates movementTwo() + movementThree() and strip() reads the global D.jobs, so nothing is state-scoped. The class is right: misleading, the product asserts something untrue. It is REFUTED on the fix, whose two stated numbers are both wrong against the real source, and whose cap does not even remove the contradiction it names. (1) 'filter D.jobs to ages under 28' leaves the 23-day and 19-day jobs and two dots past the fortnight rule. But the account is not four weeks old — it is three days old. The state's own chart starts at D.weeks[11].iso = 2026-07-13 and the reading is 2026-07-16, so 28 is not the bound; the days since the start week are. Under the proposed slice the recomputed 'haven’t moved in a fortnight' card would read 2, which is exactly as impossible as 3. (2) 'recompute D.axisMax from that slice (so the scale ends at 15d, not 45d)' contradicts its own filter: with a 23-day oldest surviving, the existing formula Math.max(45, ceil((oldest+4)/5)*5) still returns 45, and even with the 45 floor removed it returns 30. 15d is reachable from no slice the fix describes. (3) The literal '10 August' is not wrong and must not be replaced by D.readingDate + 28. 13 Jul + 28 days = 10 August; 16 Jul + 28 = 13 August. The seat's derivation would replace a correct date, honestly measured from the start of records, with a wrong one measured from today. The missing year is a genuine but separate refinement, not part of this finding's severity, and the reading line above already carries 2026 within a one-month horizon.
sharpenedFix: Bound first-run by the account's real age, not by 28. Derive accountDays = days between D.weeks[11].iso (2026-07-13) and D.bound.readingDate (2026-07-16) = 3, and build a first-run-scoped slice from it rather than mutating the global D: jobs whose age <= accountDays, axisMax derived from that slice with the Math.max(45, …) floor lifted (it exists to stop a 60-day job falling off its own chart, not to force a 45-day scale onto a three-day account), and the scale marks derived from axisMax instead of the hardcoded [0,15,30,45] list, which degenerates to the single 'today' tick at this range. Recompute all four status counts and the lead denominator from the same slice so the shared-denominator contract still holds — in a three-day-old account 'haven’t moved in a fortnight' is necessarily 0 and the fortnight marker sits past the axis end, so the strip needs a first-run treatment that says nothing has had time to sit rather than drawing a rule nothing can cross. That is a decision, not a filter, which is why the seat's one-line slice does not reach it. If a three-day fixture leaves the band too thin to be worth drawing, the honest alternative is to move the start week back so the account is genuinely a few weeks old and let every figure follow from it — but then '10 August' must move with it, since it is derived from the start week, not typed at random. Leave the date literal alone otherwise; if it is templated, template it as start week + 28 days and add the year.
breaks: A first-run slice forks the ONE-accessor-per-fact invariant the file is built on (comment above D), so it must be a state-scoped derivation passed into strip()/movementTwo(), never a second global, or a later seat finds a header and its marks disagreeing again. The coverage footer states the 9 is bound to the shipping fixture and derive-fixture.mjs fails the build on drift in bound.openCount — a first-run lead card reading anything other than 9 needs that binding claim reworded for the state, or the drift check will read the recount as drift. Re-measure after it lands: interaction-check.mjs assertions 'one dot per open job, none dropped', 'the oldest job sits inside its own axis' and the dot-collision sweep currently run against state=full only and would need first-run added, since a compressed axis packs eight or nine dots into a much shorter run and collision at 390px is the likely first casualty; audit.mjs for the strip-scale tick and fortnight-label positions at 390/768/1280/1440, since a derived mark set changes their geometry; and all seven frames re-shot, because the .ages card height changes and everything below it moves.
